html:
The Shakori were an Indigenous people of the Piedmont of present-day North Carolina, probably Siouan-speaking. By 1701 they had joined with the Eno and Adshusheer and lived in one village on the Eno River, where the English explorer John Lawson visited them.

They were small groups squeezed between the Virginia traders, the Tuscarora and the slave raids of the Carolina colony. During the 1700s their survivors merged with the Occaneechi, Saponi and Catawba, and their separate name vanished from the records.
